incidents.name: CORS / blocked browser response
incidents.symptom: Browser cannot read an API response but a direct authorised API client works.
incidents.severity: Assess customer impact and affected origin; no default incident severity.
checks: Capture origin, URL, method and browser console message.
Check OPTIONS preflight status, response headers and redirects.
Identify gateway/backend/proxy policy owner before changing configuration.
Confirm approved origin allowlist and credential rules.
escalation: API Platform Lead or backend service owner
AppSec for exceptions; incident manager if broad impact
incidents.safety: CORS is not authentication or customer-level authorisation.

incidents.name: 502 / 504 gateway failure
incidents.symptom: API gateway reports bad gateway or timeout for a Python service.
incidents.severity: Assign severity from outage scope, dependency and customer impact.
checks: Check gateway upstream target, DNS and routing.
Inspect Python service health, application exceptions and timeouts.
Check recent deployment, ingress, TLS and upstream port.
Correlate logs with trace/request ID.
escalation: SRE incident commander → Engineering Manager / Director
incidents.safety: A successful deploy does not prove a healthy upstream service.

incidents.name: LOS / LMS / reporting mismatch
incidents.symptom: Sent-back cases or state counts do not agree between systems and reporting.
incidents.severity: Assess whether workflow, financial or regulatory reporting is affected.
checks: Confirm business rules: should this state reach LMS?
Compare LOS case state/time with published event and correlation ID.
Check integration delivery, retries, rejected messages and LMS acceptance.
Reconcile source-to-mart grain, effective dates, mapping and refresh lag.
escalation: Product/BA process owner + LOS/LMS Integration Lead
incidents.safety: An HTTP 200 does not mean semantic consistency.

incidents.name: ML drift / degraded predictions
incidents.symptom: Predictive quality, score distribution or model input distributions change.
incidents.severity: Check decision materiality and model risk classification.
checks: Check availability and freshness of inference features.
Compare live input schema, missingness and feature distributions with training.
Evaluate ground-truth performance only when labels are available.
Review deployment/model version, thresholds and approved rollback rules.
escalation: Model Risk / Validation and ML Platform Manager
incidents.safety: Input drift alone does not establish that predictive performance declined.

templates.name: Business / LOS–LMS process change
checks: Approve the state-transition definition and acceptance criteria.
Validate source-to-target status mapping and idempotency.
Complete SIT for events, retries and exceptional states.
Run business UAT on journey/TAT and downstream dashboard numbers.
Reconcile loan/case grain, refresh timing and history.
Confirm rollback and cross-team release communications.

templates.name: API / Python service change
checks: Review OpenAPI contract, consumers and compatibility.
Confirm CORS origin and authentication/authorisation rules separately.
Test errors, retries, timeouts and rate limits.
Run API regression, penetration/security checks as policy requires.
Validate deployment health, traces, SLOs and rollback.

templates.name: Data contract / reporting change
checks: Confirm metric definitions, grain and denominator.
Identify upstream field contracts, owners and effective dates.
Check nulls, duplicates, late events and source reconciliation.
Run data quality tests, backfill plan and rollback.
Sign off reporting before/after comparisons.

templates.name: Model / MLOps change
checks: Version training data, features, code and model artefacts.
Review validation, fairness and model-risk requirements where applicable.
Test feature freshness, serving contract and offline/online parity.
Define rollback, champion/challenger and monitoring thresholds.
Monitor delayed-label performance and drift separately.

templates.name: Identity / security configuration
checks: Confirm requested access scope and risk classification.
Apply least privilege and separate duties as required.
Verify network, certificates, credentials and audit logging.
Run policy approval or exception workflow when needed.
Record rollback, access expiry and monitoring owner.

controls.name: CORS and origin allowlist
controls.description: Allow only approved browser origins; API must enforce user-level permissions separately.

controls.name: Authentication and authorisation
controls.description: Separate token validation, machine access, and account-level authorisation.

controls.name: Data/API contract compatibility
controls.description: Version and validate semantics, schemas, keys and effective dates.

controls.name: Source-to-report reconciliation
controls.description: Compare operational state and reporting with explicit grain and freshness.

controls.name: Model validation and drift
controls.description: Separate data drift, model risk and outcome performance.

controls.name: CI/CD and rollback
controls.description: Automate validation, deploy, observe and restore.
